title: Yasir's family
hook: the Prophet ﷺ passes the tortured family and says: patience, family of Yasir, your meeting is the garden (sirah)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sumayyah, a servant with no clan, whom Ibn Sa'd calls the first martyr in Islam. Your line was: the first to give her life.

What can be said to people you cannot rescue? Ibn Ishaq keeps one answer. The family of Yasir is being tortured in Mecca, and someone walks past who knows them: the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. He has no army, no clan strong enough to march into Makhzum's affairs and take the family home. He can't untie them. So he stops, and speaks, in a sentence short enough to carry: patience, family of Yasir, your meeting place is the garden. Today: Yasir's family.
screen: `PEOPLE YOU CANNOT RESCUE.` → `HE CAN'T UNTIE THEM.` → `PATIENCE, FAMILY OF YASIR.`

segments.voice: Look at the sentence itself. It names them. Not the believers in general, not the oppressed of Mecca: the family of Yasir. Whoever is suffering hears their own name. Then a word, sabr, patience, which in Arabic means holding steady, not waiting politely. Then a promise: the garden, the Qur'an's word for paradise, as the place where they will meet. He doesn't tell them it will stop soon. It doesn't. Ibn Sa'd says Yasir also died under the torture. Then the son. Ammar was pushed so far that he said what his torturers demanded, words against the Prophet and praise for the idols. Al-Hakim reports that he came to the Prophet weeping, and the Prophet asked him one question: how do you find your heart? Ammar said: at peace with faith. And he was told: if they come back, say it again. Commentators such as al-Tabari connect this with surah sixteen, verse one hundred six, which excuses the one forced to speak disbelief while the heart stays at rest in faith. So one family holds two kinds of faithfulness. The parents held their ground to the end. The son broke in words, kept his heart, and was not condemned for it. Both were met with mercy, not a ranking.
screen: `IT NAMES THEM.` · `SABR: HOLDING STEADY.` · `HOW DO YOU FIND YOUR HEART?` · `TWO KINDS OF FAITHFULNESS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a family you know who is carrying something heavy: an illness, a loss, a son in trouble. You may not be able to fix any of it, and neither could he, so find what you can say: their names first, then a few true words, nothing you'd have to take back. If you pray, you can pray for them by name.
Yasir's family. Yasir, Sumayyah and their son Ammar, tortured in Mecca, to whom the Prophet said: patience, your meeting place is the garden. Today's word.
Your line: patience, family of Yasir. Said to people he could not rescue, and still worth saying. Day seven hundred thirty-eight, done.

howItsDone: Muslims retell the Prophet's words to the family of Yasir in sermons on patience under hardship, and Ammar's story is a standard text in discussions of what a person forced to speak against their faith is excused.

original.note: Arabic: patience, steadfastness, holding firm; the word the Prophet used to the family of Yasir.

trapdoor: what you thought: patience means waiting quietly for things to get better.
what it means: sabr is holding steady when nothing is getting better, with your eyes on what's beyond the day.

chat.says: What did the Prophet say to the family of Yasir while they were being tortured?
options: Patience, family of Yasir; your meeting place is the garden.
Hold on, help is coming, and I will free you all tomorrow.

chat.meaning: Ibn Ishaq keeps his words: patience, family of Yasir, your meeting place is the garden. He couldn't free them, so he named them and gave hope.

al-Hakim.meaning: a hadith scholar who kept the report about Ammar

al-Tabari.meaning: an early commentator on the Qur'an
